attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Toronto.
limitations: Proposals are not completed homes. Reported units are not a forecast or a count of unique future homes.
Proximity is not walking access, service capacity, reliability or verified accessibility.
TTC only. No demand model or service-deficit claim.
Unlocated and conflicting groups are excluded from totals and remain visible in accounting.
method: 500 m EPSG:26917 grid. Straight-line distance from each qualified proposal address point. At least four scheduled departures in each hour at one stop on one route-direction.

addresses.name: Address Points - 4326.geojson
addresses.notes:
The One Address Repository data set provides a point representation for over 500,000 addresses within the City of Toronto. Each address point is described with a series of attributes including street number, street name, address type, feature class and real world coordinates.

All address points have a position on the correct side of the street, and are correctly positioned relative to neighbouring addresses. They are positioned within the parcel or the building footprint.

applications.name: Development Applications
applications.notes:
This dataset lists all currently active (open) and inactive (closed) Community Planning applications and Committee of Adjustment applications received by the City between January 1st 2008 till present.

For more info, see:
[Application Information Centre](https://www.toronto.ca/aic/)


[Development Applications - Development Projects](http://app.toronto.ca/AIC/index.do)

projects.licence_basis: Publisher dataset page explicitly links Open Government Licence – Toronto; API metadata may be unspecified.
projects.name: Development Pipeline
projects.notes: The Development Pipeline examines how and where the city has grown over the past five years and provides insight on how it will continue to develop in the near future. The Development Pipeline enables City Planning to track urban growth, monitor development trends, and measure progress towards municipal and provincial housing targets. The Development Pipeline bulletin is published annually and the dashboard is updated quarterly on a best-effort basis. A subset of the Development Pipeline information is used to create this dashboard.
